title: Evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in pregnant and breastfeeding women.
ehr_evidence: An anonymous online questionnaire created via Google Forms was addressed to vaccinated women from Slovakia and Czech Republic, and was used to collect data.
summary: Evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine safety and efficacy in pregnant and breastfeeding women using a self-reported online questionnaire.
key_findings: Breastfeeding women experienced higher adverse event rates than pregnant women.

Significant differences in adverse event incidence were observed for fatigue (RR 1.230, 95% CI 1.051-1.444, P=0.0098), headache (RR 1.822, 95% CI 1.379-2.418, P<0.0001), myalgia (RR 1.633, 95% CI 1.269-2.110, P<0.0001), chills (RR 2.027, P<0.0001), subfebrile temperature ≤38°C (RR 1.697, 95% CI 1.240-2.335, P=0.0007), arthralgia (RR 1.924, 95% CI 1.340-2.776, P=0.0002), fever >38°C (RR 6.410, 95% CI 2.890-14.30, P<0.0001), and shivers (RR 2.204, 95% CI 1.264-3.863, P=0.0049).
Menstrual cycle bleeding disorders occurred in 0.7% of breastfeeding women after the first dose and 0.5% after the second dose.
93.1% of pregnancies were carried to term, 5.6% late preterm, 0.9% moderate preterm, and 0.3% very preterm.
Vaccine efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 infection was 96.3%.
Serious adverse event incidence was 0.3% (7 SAEs in 2165 respondents).
population: pregnant and breastfeeding women (n=2192) from Slovakia and Czech Republic
limitations: self-reported data without trained personnel verification
efficacy analysis limited by voluntary post-vaccination isolation
data collected before the Omicron variant era
only original monovalent mRNA vaccines assessed
